p: A quick word on getting the best from your session: talk constantly. Free-roam games are won by teams that call out what they can see, cover each other's backs and stick together, so the chattiest squads usually top the scoreboard. Don't be shy about asking the staff for a recap of the controls if you missed something in the briefing.

Once you're done, Guildford has a surprising amount packed into a small space. The castle grounds, near the top of town, have pretty gardens and the Norman keep, which opens to visitors in the warmer months and has views over the rooftops. Tucked in the grounds is a statue of Alice going through the looking glass, a nod to Lewis Carroll, who spent time in Guildford and is buried in the town.

Down by the river, Dapdune Wharf is a National Trust site on the River Wey Navigations, telling the story of the barges that once carried goods up and down the waterway. It's a lovely spot for a riverside walk, and in the warmer months you can often take a boat trip from the town. Guildford Cathedral, the striking red-brick building up on Stag Hill, is worth a look too.

If you've still got energy after all that action, the Surrey Hills are right on the doorstep. Newlands Corner and St Martha's Hill, a short drive east, have big views and great walks, perfect for blowing away the cobwebs before heading home.
